supports: Giacomelli, Perrotta, Scandone, Scarpati, Episodes 26(3) 2003: eruption phases, column heights, fall rate, roof collapse, victim counts
quotes: the two Plinys observed the cloud at the seventh hour of the day (1 PM). We must presume that the eruption began sometime earlier

They estimated that the eruption column rose from an height of 14 km to 26 km during the emission of white pumice and then to 32 km during the emission of grey pumice immediately before the deposition of pyroclastic flows.
a lower part of well-sorted white pumice and an upper part of gray pumice dispersed to the southeast of the volcano

The rate of deposition in the city ranged from 15 cm per hour in open areas to 25/30 cm per hour in places accumulating additional pyroclasts rolling from the steeper roofs. Within six hours from the beginning of the eruption the roofs and part of the walls of the buildings had collapsed under the pumice load.
the pumice fall deposit, generally 3 m thick, totally buried the lower part of the buildings

394 corpses were found in the pumice fall deposit and 650 in the pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) deposit. So a total of 1044 victims were recovered inside 2/3 of the city of Pompeii (the excavated part).
